items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip cleaning sparse prefill MQA logits
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.
This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel.

This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty`
and the fill is removed.

## Safety

The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside
`[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial
load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged.

## Results

MI355X, TP=4, rank 0, comparable before/after captures:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP32 fill launches | 18,162 | **0** |
| FP32 fill GPU time | 1,250.2 ms | **0 ms** |
| MQA-logits launches | 18,108 | 17,930 |

The removed fill was **0.89% of total GPU kernel time**. In the sample below it

items.title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Use FlashKDA for KDA chunked prefill (1.7-3.8x faster than the Triton chunk path)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Use **FlashKDA** (`vllm._flashkda_C`, already built and used by Kimi-K3) for GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA chunked prefill instead of the ~15-kernel Triton `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` path.

FlashKDA implements the same bounded-gate KDA recurrence GLM-5.3-Flash uses (`lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (g + dt_bias))`, in-kernel q/k l2norm, raw beta logits), so it is a drop-in. On GB300 per KDA layer (H=16/rank, D=128, `bench/flashkda_vs_chunk.py`):

| shape | Triton chunk path | FlashKDA |
|---|---|---|
| 8 x 2048 tokens | 183 us | 49 us |
| 4 x 8192 | 555 us | 146 us |
| 1 x 16384 | 1371 us | 787 us |

Selection: automatic when supported (SM90/SM10x/SM12x, bf16, head_dim 128, bounded gate); `additional_config.kda_prefill_backend = triton` keeps the old path (`flashkda` forces it). The output is written straight into the layer buffer (no merge copy) and the pre-sigmoid beta cast is not needed on this path. Spec-decode tokens themselves keep the Triton recurrent kernel (`num_accepted_tokens` rollback); in a step that carries both, FlashKDA runs the prefill segment into a workspace buffer and the outputs are scattered back by `non_spec_token_indx` / `spec_token_indx` (same scheme as the Kimi-K3 KDA layer; the merge writes straight into `core_attn_out`).

```python
(req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
```

For a hybrid (multi-group) model attached to a KV connector, `get_block_ids` returns one list per KV cache group, so the first failed remote chunk load kills EngineCore with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1, got N)` — observed live on GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 (6 groups) with dfkv/Mooncake-style stores; the same crash reproduces with any KV connector on a hybrid model.

Even without the crash, the single-group recovery semantics (truncate `num_computed_tokens` at the first failed block and resume) are unsound for hybrid models: state groups (mamba) depend on the full-attention group's boundary state, so resuming one group at a partial prefix while another group failed produces silently inconsistent KV.

This PR makes hybrid requests replay from zero with every participating group's prefix hashes invalidated:

- Coverage per group uses the engine's own outer-spec rule (AttentionSpec scaled by DCP; other specs unscaled) over groups that participate in prefix caching, considering only the possibly-externally-computed prefix.
- A failure in any group invalidates **every** participating group's cached block hashes via `kv_cache_manager.evict_blocks` (hash-only: receive buffers the connector still owns are not returned to the allocator).
- `recompute` policy (default): the request is marked `skip_reading_prefix_cache`, RUNNING requests are preempted through the normal `_preempt_request` path back into the waiting queue, and async `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests reset to zero so the existing finished-recv flow frees their groups.
- `fail` policy reports the affected requests and eviction set without touching recompute state; single-group requests keep the existing longest-valid-prefix and shared-block optimizations unchanged.

No wire, connector, or allocator contracts change; non-hybrid mod

items.title: [PCP][DCP] Declare FlashMLASparse MTP support at CP interleave > 1
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Make MTP reachable for PCP+DCP sparse-MLA prefillers behind NIXL P/D.

With `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` and a `NixlConnector`, `VllmConfig.adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` raises `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the block size (64) for block-level alignment of the DCP → decoder transfer. `cp_utils.validate_cp_support` then asserts `supports_mtp_with_cp_non_trivial_interleave_size` on every attention impl whenever a speculative config is present:

```
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashMLASparseImpl.
```

The flag is declared `False` in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py` and set `True` by no backend in the tree, so MTP + DCP>1 + NIXL is unreachable on main for every sparse-MLA model. This declares it on `FlashMLASparseImpl` only.

**Why this should be safe on this impl:** the mixed-fp8 path processes all scheduled query tokens together, and its slot mapping and sparse-index conversion both thread `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` through (`flashmla_sparse.py` passes it into the DCP index conversion at both call sites). Nothing in the impl assumes interleave 1 except the capability declaration itself.

## Status — draft, validation in progress

Measured on H200, GLM-5.3, PCP8+DCP8+EP8 (TP1) prefiller → TP8+EP8 decoder over NIXL, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`:

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

#56107 runs the DFlash/DSpark drafter **replicated** under PCP, but once the process also runs DCP > 1, three places still treat the draft's KV as DCP-sharded. The draft then either fails config validation or runs the sharded attention path over a replicated KV:

```
ValidationError: tp_size=1 must be divisible by dcp_size=8
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashAttentionImpl
RuntimeError: mha_fwd ... scheduler_metadata must have shape (metadata_size)   # _forward_with_dcp on a replicated KV
```

Hit with DSpark7 at PCP8+DCP8+EP8 (TP1) prefiller → TP8+EP8 decoder over NIXL P/D (which raises `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to 64), GLM-5.3 on H200.

## Fix (one commit, ~60 lines)

- **Draft `ParallelConfig`** — `DFlashSpeculator` collapsed only the PCP axis, leaving `dcp=8, pcp=1`, which `ParallelConfig` rejects. Collapse DCP with it (`dcp // pcp`).
- **KV-spec geometry** — `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size` / `dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec` scaled any attention group by the process DCP. An `Attention` layer now records whether the config it was built under has DCP (`AttentionSpec.dcp_sharded`, default `True`), and the helpers leave a replicated group's geometry alone.
- **Attention impl / FA builder** — took `dcp_world_size` from `get_dcp_group()`. A layer built under a config with no DCP now reports 1 and skips the DCP forward path.
- **`check_attention_cp_compatibility`** — applied the interleave/LSE impl checks to every layer in the forward context; scope them to `target_layer_names` as the PCP backend check already is. (Supersedes #56737.)

Target layers are built under the target config and are unchanged: `dcp_sharded=True`, `dcp_world_size` still matches the group.

items.title: [Security] Cap Qwen-VL video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL video samplers ignore `num_frames` and bound sampling on request-controlled `max_frames` and `fps`. A client can raise those knobs through `media_io_kwargs` and force the frontend to decode every source frame. This applies the same class-level ceilings already used by the GLMGA sampler (`_MAX_FRAMES`, `_MAX_FPS`), so a request may lower the sample count but cannot raise it past 768 frames or 30 fps.

## Changes
- `vllm/multimodal/video.py`: clamp `max_frames` and `fps` in `Qwen2VLVideoBackend` and `Qwen3VLVideoBackend`.
- `tests/multimodal/test_video.py`: regression tests that oversized `max_frames`/`fps` stay at the class ceiling, a lower request still wins, and default sampling is unchanged.

## Codepath coverage
- Sink is `compute_frames_index_to_sample` on both Qwen backends. OpenCV, TorchCodec, PyNvVideoCodec, and DeepStream all call that method, so every codec is covered.
- Chat completions, embeddings, responses, tokenize, invocations, batch, and offline `LLM` all reach the same `MediaConnector` → `VideoMediaIO` → registered sampler chain.
- `video/jpeg` `load_base64` does not use these samplers (it keys off `num_frames`). The Rust frontend rejects `media_io_kwargs` and is unaffected.
- Sibling loaders (Molmo2, glm5next, OpenPangu) have their own open PRs and are not changed here.

## Duplicate-work check
Open/merged PRs searched for Qwen backends, `max_frames`, `media_io_kwargs`, and video sampling caps.
- #51969 clamps `num_frames` in `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` only; these samplers ignore `num_frames`.
- #54935 capped GLMGA, not Qwen.
- #55727, #56207, and #56390 target glm5next, Molmo2, and OpenPangu respectively.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CU

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][PCP] Scope CP impl checks to the target model's layers
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`check_attention_cp_compatibility()` iterates every `AttentionLayerBase` in `static_forward_context`. That context is shared with the draft model, and a DFlash/DSpark draft collapses PCP and DCP (its `ParallelConfig` is `pcp=1, dcp=1`), so its KV is never CP-sharded — yet its full-attention layers were being held to the **target's** interleave:

```
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashAttentionImpl.
```

Reached with DSpark7 at PCP8+DCP8+EP8 behind NIXL P/D (interleave auto-adjusted to 64), on GLM-5.3 / H200, once the draft `ParallelConfig` was made valid by #56723.

## Fix

The caller (`gpu/model_runner.py`) already passes `target_attn_layer_names`, and the PCP backend check in the same loop already scopes itself to them (`check_pcp`). The two `impl` assertions — MTP at interleave > 1, and LSE-for-DCP — did not. This scopes them the same way: layers outside the target set are skipped, exactly as they already were for the backend check. Behaviour for target layers is unchanged; `target_layer_names=None` (the `gpu_model_runner.py` caller) still checks everything.

## Relationship to other PRs

- #56723 makes the DSpark draft config valid under PCP+DCP (this assertion is the next thing that fires).
- #56722 declares the flag on `FlashMLASparseImpl` for the *target's* sparse-MLA layers, which do need it at interleave 64. This PR is about not applying that requirement to the draft's non-sharded layers.

## Test Plan

- Unit test (no GPU) exercising the function with a fake forward context containing a target layer whose impl declares the flag and a draft layer whose impl does not: passes when `target_layer_names` excludes the draft layer, and still fails when `target_layer_names=None`. Being added.
- End-to-end: DSpark7 at PCP8+DCP8+EP8 → TP8+EP8 over NIXL, gsm8k + Prometheus-counter acceptance; queued, result to be posted here.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Test 1280-token GLM sparse-MLA int32 slot overflow
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Keep GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA prefill from overflowing signed int32 when the KV row stride is 512 and the serving page is 1280 tokens.

#53906 already promotes `slot` via `_sparse_kv_row_offset` and tests the native hybrid 640-token page (overflow at block 6554). On gfx942 we align hybrid 1152 up to `index_kpool*64=256`, so serving `block_size` is **1280**. Then:

```
INT32_MAX / (1280 * 512) = 3276.8
```

A production dump on MI325X TP4 first assigned MLA `new_block_ids` 3278–3280 on the dying chunked-prefill step (`computed=46080`, `scheduled=3840`). Without the int64 promote, `_sparse_attn_prefill_ragged_kernel` does `slot * kv_stride_n` in int32 and Memory-access-faults.

## Changes

Parametrize `test_sparse_prefill_kv_row_offset_does_not_overflow_int32` with both layouts:

- 640-token pages, first overflowing block 6554 (existing)
- 1280-token pages, first overflowing block 3277 (serving)

No kernel change. Main already has `_sparse_kv_row_offset`.

## Test

`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py` (ROCm).

items.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Skinny GEMM dispatch for tiny-M decode projections
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

At tiny M (1–4 rows) the dense projections on DeepSeek-V4.1's decode path are dispatch-mismatched: MXFP8 CuTeDSL and BF16 cuBLAS kernels sized for bulk traffic run weight-bound rounds. This PR adds a shape-keyed skinny dispatch table (SM100/B200 only, TP8 shapes) that swaps in the measured winners exactly where they win — a Triton SIMT GEMM for the three MXFP8 projections, CuTe skinny for the BF16 indexer/lm_head projections, and ll_bf16 dotprod for the FP32 compressor scores, 20 (shape, M) cells in total.

Semantics are preserved exactly: MXFP8 candidates keep the per-32-element E8M0 activation scale and FP8 rounding (`round_mx` in the SIMT kernel reproduces the baseline MXFP8 quantization), and FP32 compressor outputs stay FP32. Everything falls back to the original kernels off-table, off-device, non-BF16 input, with LoRA attached, with a bias, or under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. The dispatch runs at model init for the three unquantized BF16 modules (K3/GLM-5.2 quant-method replacement precedent) and at the model-layer call sites for the fused/wo_a/compressor paths, so module forward and any wrappers are untouched off the table.
